question.questionText: If we_______ in a town, life would be better.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The sentence 'If we_______ in a town, life would be better.' is a conditional sentence. In this case, it is the second conditional, which is used to talk about unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future. The structure for the second conditional is: If + past simple, would + base verb. Therefore, the correct verb form to use after 'If we' is the past simple.
  • had lived (verb (past perfect)): 'Had lived' is the past perfect tense, which is used in the third conditional (If + had + past participle, would have + past participle) to talk about unreal situations in the past. It is not correct here.
  • lived (verb (past simple)): 'Lived' is the past simple tense, which is the correct form for the second conditional structure.
  • would live (modal verb + base verb): 'Would live' is used in the main clause of the conditional sentence, not after 'if'.
  • live (verb (present simple)): 'Live' is the present simple tense, which is used in the zero conditional (If + present simple, present simple) for general truths, not hypothetical situations.
Related structure or vocabulary: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb. Used for unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future.

Cấu trúc của câu điều kiện loại 2 là: If + quá khứ đơn, would + động từ nguyên thể. Vì vậy, động từ sau 'If we' phải ở thì quá khứ đơn.
  • had lived (động từ (quá khứ hoàn thành)): 'Had lived' là thì quá khứ hoàn thành, dùng trong câu điều kiện loại 3 (If + had + V3, would have + V3) để nói về những tình huống không có thật trong quá khứ. Không phù hợp trong trường hợp này.
  • lived (động từ (quá khứ đơn)): 'Lived' là thì quá khứ đơn, là dạng đúng cho cấu trúc câu điều kiện loại 2.
  • would live (động từ khuyết thiếu + động từ nguyên thể): 'Would live' được dùng ở mệnh đề chính của câu điều kiện, không dùng sau 'if'.

question.questionText: We _____ you if we have time.

The blank in the sentence 'We _____ you if we have time.' requires the correct verb tense to match the conditional structure. The phrase 'if we have time' is in the present simple tense, which indicates a real possibility in the future. In the first conditional, we use 'will' + base verb in the main clause and present simple in the if-clause to talk about real and possible situations in the future.
  • would phone (modal verb + base verb): 'Would phone' is used in the second conditional (if + past simple, would + base verb), which talks about unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future. It does not fit here because the if-clause uses present simple.
  • had phoned (past perfect): 'Had phoned' is the past perfect tense, used in the third conditional (if + past perfect, would have + past participle) to talk about unreal situations in the past. It is not suitable here.
  • phoned (simple past): 'Phoned' is the simple past tense. It does not fit the structure of the first conditional, which requires 'will' + base verb in the main clause.
  • will phone (future simple): 'Will phone' is the correct form for the main clause in the first conditional, used to express a real possibility in the future.
Related structure or vocabulary: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb. Used to talk about real and possible situations in the future.
